title: What We Believe
content:
All Saints’ Church is rooted in the historic interpretation of the Christian Bible—which is summarized in the words of the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds. Our specific theological convictions are expressed in the Thirty-Nine Articles of the Anglican Communion. All Saints' Church is part of the Anglican Church in North America and is under Bishop Chris Warner of the Diocese of the Mid-Atlantic.

Foundational Documents

  • The Holy Bible (ESV)
  • The Nicene Creed
  • The Apostles’ Creed

Additional Documents

  • Book of Common Prayer
  • Thirty-Nine Articles of Religion
  • The Jerusalem Declaration
  • To Be a Christian: An Anglican Catechism

title: Our History
content:
Timeline

All Saints’ roots date back to the first Anglican church established in Prince William County in 1667 when a chapel was built on the banks of Quantico Creek in Dumfries.

January 1, 1980

St. Martin's, a mission church in the Dumfries-Quantico area started in 1955 by Trinity Episcopal in Manassas, and Holy Spirit, a mission church in Dale City started in 1963 by St. Margaret’s, merge to form All Saints’. The bishop proposed the merger since St. Martin’s had a building, but no priest, while Holy Spirit had a priest, but no building. Conditions of the merger included calling a new vicar and building a new church in Dale City. The Rev. Chuck Stein, who had been vicar of Holy Spirit, continued as interim vicar of the combined congregations until he retired on Dec. 31, 1980. Paula Woods and Robert Pritchard followed as interim vicars.

Feb. 17, 1980

All Saints’ holds its first service at the old St. Martin’s building in Triangle.

December 1981

The Rev. John A.M. Guernsey called as All Saints’ new vicar

March 3, 1983

All Saints’ holds its first service in its new building on Saratoga Lane in Dale City

April 10, 1983

All Saints’ is dedicated

AUGUST 1985

The Rev. Whis Hays and the Rev. Mary Hays join All Saints’ as associate vicars

SEPTEMBER 1987

Mary Hays leaves for Truro Church in Fairfax

Jan. 31, 1988

All Saints’ gains full parish status

JUNE 1989

The Rev. Valarie Whitcomb joins All Saints’ as associate rector

SEPTEMBER 1989

Whis Hayes leaves All Saints’ to start Rock the World Youth Mission Alliance in Ambridge, PA

1995

The original prayer room built as part of a six-room expansion

May 2001

All Saints’ purchases 28 acres of land on Gideon Drive in Woodbridge next to Hylton Chapel to build a new, larger church to hold the growing congregation

NOV. 2005

The Rev. Mark Brown joins All Saints’ as associate rector

Dec. 10, 2006

Congregation votes to leave The Episcopal Church, becoming part of the Anglican Diocese of North Kigezi within the Church of Uganda

Sept. 2007

John Guernsey consecrated as bishop, taking on new diocesan duties while remaining All Saints’ rector

June 23, 2009

All Saints’ transfers out of the Church of Uganda and into the newly established Anglican Church in North America

SEPTEMBER 2009

Valarie Whitcomb retires as associate rector

April 2010

The Rev. Dan Morgan called to become All Saints’ next rector

June 13, 2010

John Guernsey officially steps down as All Saints’ rector after 28 years to devote all his attention as the bishop of the then-Diocese of the Holy Spirit in the Anglican Church of North America

APRIL 1, 2011

The Rev. Alex Leighton joins All Saints’ as associate rector

September 2011

New All Saints’ church opens on Gideon Drive

JUNE 2015

Mark Brown retires as associate rector

JUNE 2018

Alex Leighton leaves All Saints’ to plant a church in Bozeman, Montana

August 31, 2018

Dan Morgan leaves All Saints’ to become rector at St. Luke's in Copley, Ohio

March 7, 2019

The Rev. Scott Bailey called as All Saints’ next rector

JAN, 2021

The Rev. Jedd Trenum becomes All Saints’ associate rector

DEC. 2025

The Rev. Maryanna Stumbaugh becomes All Saints’ associate rector. She replaces Jedd Trenum, who became vicar at The Anglican Church of the Valley in Staunton, VA.

AUG. 2026

The Rev. Patricio Rojas joins All Saints’ staff as the associate rector for Spanish-Language Ministry.

title: The Jerusalem Cross
content:
Behind the altar is the Jerusalem cross that has hung in that same spot both here in our new building and in our former building on Saratoga Lane since that church was first built.

The Jerusalem Cross is a Christian symbol consisting of a large cross surrounded by four smaller crosses, one in each quadrant. Over the years, the Jerusalem cross has acquired a number of interpretations. The five crosses can symbolize the five wounds of Christ during the Passion; the Pentateuch (the first five books of the Bible); and, perhaps the first five Christian churches. The four smaller crosses are also said to be symbolic of the four Gospels proclaimed to the four corners of the earth, beginning in Jerusalem; the large cross in the center symbolizes the person of Christ.

This cross is a very special symbol for All Saints’ Church—it speaks to who we are. As Jesus told His disciples to go forth and proclaim the Gospel to all the world, we, too, are charged to spread the Good News of Christ in our own world, in Woodbridge, from Saratoga Lane and Gideon Drive. When we see the Jerusalem cross, we are reminded that our own church is not to be a self-contained entity, but to be welcoming and to serve, reaching out in boldness to our community.

We are called to “love and serve the Lord” and All Saints’ has been a church that “equips the Saints (us) for ministry.” Now we are to be a church “overflowing with God’s love and healing power.” Christ, symbolically the center of the Jerusalem cross, reminds us that He equips us, we are filled with the power of the Holy Spirit, and He wants us to use our gifts, our training, and His power to love, grow and serve in His name.

title: Our Vestry
content:
The Vestry currently consists of the Rector and nine elected lay members. Each elected lay member serves a three-year term. The Vestry provides oversight in the temporal activities, business affairs, and property of the Church; assists the Rector in providing spiritual leadership and oversight of the ecclesiastical affairs of the Church; prays regularly for the Church and its mission; and serves as a resource for godly counsel, biblical wisdom, and accountability for the Rector and other clergy of the Church.

title: Safeguarding
content:
All Saints’ Church takes seriously the protection of our youngest saints as well as vulnerable adults. We require extensive training for those individuals working with our children.

We have researched and established “Best Practices” to protect God’s children which include:

  • Careful screening of all staff and volunteers who work with children (applications, personal reference checks, national sexual offender registry and criminal background checks, etc.)
  • Interaction and Monitoring Guidelines (two-person rule at all times)
  • A Coded Check In-Check Out System with one entrance to the Children’s Wing

Please contact Tara Pedersen, Children’s Ministry Director, for more information on our safeguards or to register for one of our upcoming workshops. Childcare is available upon request.

View the complete Diocese of the Mid-Atlantic policy here.

title: Sunday Services
content:
Almighty God, to you all hearts are open, all desires known, and from you no secrets are hid:
Cleanse the thoughts of our hearts by the inspiration of your Holy Spirit,
that we may perfectly love you, and worthily magnify your holy Name;
through Christ our Lord.Amen.

The Collect for Purity, Book of Common Prayer (p. 123)

All are invited to worship with us in our Anglican tradition of Holy Eucharist each Sunday at 8:15 a.m. or 11 a.m. Our services generally last 90 minutes; nursery care and Children’s Church are available during both. We include a mix of contemporary music and hymns in our worship. Our prayers are found in the Book of Common Prayer (2019). Take a look at the order of service for Sundays here.

You can expect to see a range of dress from casual to formal. Visitors are welcome to dress as they are most comfortable attending a Sunday morning service. However you choose to join us, you will be welcome!

Service Information:

Sunday Service Times

  • 8:15 a.m.
  • 11 a.m.
    Children’s Church is offered at both services for children age 3 through 5th grade. They can be checked into the Children’s Wing before the service starts. Children are brought back into the Sanctuary after the sermon for Holy Eucharist.

Sunday school Hour

Sunday School Hour is on Sundays from 9:45 a.m. - 10:45 a.m. (between the services). We study various aspects of the Bible or biblical principles. Course topics vary throughout the seasons. Children (PreK through 12th grade) also participate in this learning opportunity, attending Sunday School during Sunday School Hour.

Nursery Care

Nursery care is available during both services and during Sunday School Hour.

Building Accessibility

We want everyone to have access to our services, therefore our building has:

  • Accessible parking convenient to front and rear entrances.
  • Ramps from street to curb level with no additional steps to enter the building.
  • Accessible bathrooms (grab rails, larger stalls and angled mirrors).
  • Exterior doors that, when fully extended, will lock in the open position, allowing a guest to enter without having to hold the door open.

We would be happy to address any questions or concerns you might have. Please feel free to call our main office at 703-670-0093.

title: Baptism
content:
This public declaration of faith in Jesus Christ takes place during Sunday morning worship on or near five occasions each year: Pentecost, All Saints' Day, The Baptism of Our Lord (the Sunday after the Epiphany), and Easter Eve (a Saturday evening service). In addition, baptism usually takes place once during the summer months. Through either the pouring on of water, or immersion in water, we are cleansed of our sins, incorporated into the Body of Christ, and called to ministry in the Name of Jesus.

Almighty and everlasting Father, in your great mercy you saved Noah and his family in the Ark from the destruction of the flood, prefiguring the Sacrament of Holy Baptism. Look mercifully upon these your servants. Wash and sanctify them through your Holy Spirit, that they may be delivered from destruction and received into the Ark of Christ’s Church; and being steadfast in faith, joyful through hope, and rooted in love, they may pass through the turbulent floods of this troublesome world and come into the land of everlasting life, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen. (BCP, 2019)

title: Prayer
content:
Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.

Philippians 4:6

All Saints’ Church has been called by God to be a “House of Prayer.” We welcome your prayer requests regarding any and all concerns or praise reports for you, your family members or friends.

Prayer Requests

All prayer requests will be prayed for by the intercessory team for two weeks. Please be specific about your request (e.g. healing of cancer, etc.) and, if submitting for someone else, please note your relationship to this person, (e.g. yourself or your mother, son, uncle, cousin, neighbor, co-worker, etc.) Please note, we would love to receive a follow-up report, whether more prayer is needed or your prayers are answered. Contact Deacon Julie (jtilton@allsaintswoodbridge.org) with your feedback or submit a praise report online. We love to give God praise for answered prayer!

(Boxes with an asterisk must be filled in).

Other Ways to Receive Prayer

During the Prayers of the People, there will be a time for the congregation to participate aloud by lifting up personal names.

People in need of prayer are always encouraged to seek prayer from prayer teams located at the back of the church during Communion.

We want to praise God with you for all His good gifts!

title: Children
content:
...so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith—that you, being rooted and grounded in love...

Ephesians 3:17

The Children’s Ministry at All Saints’ Church serves infants, toddlers, and children through the fifth grade. While we recognize and affirm that the spiritual development of children is first and foremost a parent’s responsibility, our church is poised and ready to assist! We seek to partner with you and support your family in training up children to love and serve the Lord each day of their lives. Children are welcomed, valued, protected, and lovingly cared for while they learn who Jesus is, how to follow Him and how the truths of the Bible can help them to make Godly choices. Our dedicated Children’s Ministry team is committed to helping children:

  • Understand that God earnestly desires a personal, meaningful and growing relationship through Jesus with them
  • Read, know, and love God’s word
  • Learn how to engage in daily prayer and worship
  • Experience God’s presence through the Holy Spirit as an integral part of their lives
  • Voluntarily participate in acts of service
  • Become committed to using their spiritual gifts
  • Grow in Christ-like character

REGISTER FOR THE 2026-2027 CHILDREN’S MINISTRY SCHOOL YEAR HERE:

News regarding Children’s Ministry

Children’s Church

During both our 8:15 a.m. and 11 a.m. services, children ages 3 through the fifth grade are invited to the Children’s Wing for Children’s Church. Our trained team leads the children in engaging, interactive, and age-appropriate Bible lessons. Your kids won't want to miss a moment of the fun! Children return to the adult service at the passing of the peace in time to receive communion or a blessing.

Sunday School

Upon turning three, a child may “graduate” from the Toddler Nursery to the Pre-Kindergarten classroom. Sunday School is offered from 9:45-10:45 a.m. for ages Pre-K through the fifth grade in the Children's Wing. Colorful classrooms provide a welcoming setting for children to engage in a small-group experience. While exploring the truths of God’s word, children play games, create crafts, enjoy a snack, pray and praise God together!

title: Nursery
content:
All Saints’ Church offers three unique nurseries for the children from birth through the age of four: Infant, Wobbler, and Toddler. Each space is thoughtfully equipped with developmentally appropriate toys and books, and lovingly staffed by paid employees and dedicated volunteers. The nurseries are located just down the hall from the Sanctuary inside the Children's Wing. Doors that allow the top to open separately connect the three nurseries; this helps us keep a steady flow of communication between our three different areas for little ones. We think you'll find each nursery just right for meeting the developmental needs of the children for which it was designed!

Nurseries are open on Sunday mornings for the 8:15 a.m. service, the Discipleship hour (9:45-10:45 a.m.) and for the 11 a.m. church service. The infant nursery is also open for large church events for which arrangements have been specifically made. For other events during the week infants may be dropped off for care in the toddler nursery.

Paid staff and volunteers are trained prior to working in the nurseries. Occasionally, mature teens work alongside experienced infant nursery volunteers or staff.

If you have questions or would like more information, please contact Tara Pedersen (tpedersen@allsaintswoodbridge.org) or Asteir Shokai (ashokai@allsaintswoodbridge.org) at 703-670-0093.

Parents are welcome in any of our nurseries for the purposes of nursing, feeding, changing, or comforting their children at any time!

Registering Your Child in Our Nurseries

When first visiting All Saints' Church, you will be asked to register your children to let us know more about your children and how you would like us to care for them. Please visit the Welcome/Check-in center (booth just outside the children's wing entrance) to register your child or you can fill out the registration form.

Register Your Child

Nursery Check-in

To check in your registered child, please see the Welcome/Check-In center on Sunday mornings. To keep our children safe, parents and children will be given matching ID bracelets. Children will be released only after staff has made sure that the child's and parent's bracelets match.

All Saints' Sick-Child Policy

Please help us keep our nurseries a safe and healthy environment for all our little ones by not bringing your children to the nurseries when they are sick. Please read All Saints' Sick-Child Nursery policy. Thanks for your cooperation and understanding!

Infant Nursery

The infant nursery is located immediately inside the doors of the Children's Wing. It provides a calm and comfy environment with several cushy rockers for parents to rock or feed their little ones. Diaper changing tables are available, stocked with plenty of diapers should parents have a need. Baby swings and exer-saucers make this nursery a perfect place for little ones to experience the love of Jesus. Parents have the ability to listen to the service live via closed-circuit audio while in this nursery.

Wobbler Nursery

We consider wobblers those children who are actively mobile, but not quite full-fledged toddlers yet (ages 1 to 2 is a good starting point.) Wobblers have very different needs from infants and toddlers and we are pleased to have created an inviting space just for them!

The Wobbler Nursery sits between the Infant and Toddler nurseries. Wobblers will delight in playing with colorful soft-form tunnels and slides to chunky interactive toys. A fully stocked changing table and rocking chair that this is a practical space too for parents who need to use the nursery. Wobblers will be invited to sit on the snack blanket for a finger-food snack (Cheerios or similar) and will be offered sippy cups of juice.

The Wobbler Nursery is open during the 9:45-10:45 a.m. Discipleship hour and the 11 a.m. service. During the 8:15 service, parents may leave their wobbler-aged child for care in our Toddler Nursery.

Toddler Nursery

Our Toddler Nursery is adjacent to the Infant and Wobbler nurseries. It is open each Sunday morning during the 8:15 and 11 a.m. services, as well as during the 9:45 -10:45 a.m. Discipleship hour.

The Toddler Nursery is equipped with toys and books suitable for various toddler ages, a diaper changing table, extra supplies such as diapers, baby wipes, a table and chairs for play and for snack time (apple juice and either graham, animal, or goldfish crackers), comfortable chairs for holding and comforting children. In the toddler nursery, your child will be welcomed in to experience the love of Jesus. We offer free-play, kid-friendly worship music, and occasional age-appropriate lessons, crafts, or activities. A toddler-sized toilet is available in the restroom within the Toddler Nursery. Once a child has reached the age of four, they may “graduate” to the Pre-K class during the Sunday School hour.

title: Adult Formation
content:
At All Saints’ Church, Adult Formation is at the heart of our ministry.
We believe in nurturing spiritual growth and deepening the faith of our parishioners
through various avenues of formation.
We offer a wide range of opportunities
for learning, discussion, and reflection.
We hold regular Bible studies, small groups, and workshops
that delve into scripture, theology, and practical applications of faith.
We aim to equip and empower adults to fully embrace their call
as followers of Christ in their daily lives.

We provide a variety of Adult Formation opportunities during the Sunday School Hour (9:45-10:45 a.m.) and throughout the week! Take a look at our current offerings. Have questions? Please contact Trina McCarthy at adultdiscipleship@allsaintswoodbridge.org.

Current Offerings on Sunday & During the Week

All Saints’ Church Adult Formation seeks to meet all curious seekers, newly baptized Christians, and seasoned Christians right where they are to support all people in becoming more like our Savior Jesus Christ. Offerings are published in our various church communications. Courses change throughout the year, but our purpose remains steadfast. On Sunday mornings, we conduct classes in small groups to promote participation to the extent each individual is comfortable (and to enjoy coffee or tea – your preference!).

An Encouragement for Daily Bible Reading

All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work. (2 Timothy 3.16-17)

Daily reading of the Bible has so many benefits. We learn. We are cautioned. We are corrected and/or redirected. We are trained in what God says is right. We are equipped for all good works God has prepared in advance for us to do (Ephesians 2:10). Reading Scripture and asking God for the wisdom to apply it in our everyday life ultimately helps us to become the disciples Jesus commands us to be in the Great Commission (Matthew 28:18-19).

Nowhere in the Bible does God say how much to read or hear each time we look into His Scripture. So whether you read (or listen to) a little or a lot of Scripture on a daily basis, please do make it a habit.

May you receive the greatest benefit of all: knowing God and drawing closer to Him.

“rooted and growing”: a monday-through-saturday bible reading tool

Small Group Information

How Does A Small Group Work?

Small groups typically meet once a week in someone’s home for informal worship, Bible study, prayer and fellowship. Together the group agrees to meet for a specific period of time, perhaps 3 months or so. A group of six may come together with a vision to grow to 12 or more and multiply.

What is a small group?

  • A place to learn more about what the Bible says and how to apply it to your life
  • A place to receive support from others during the difficult times we all occasionally experience
  • A safe environment to share and ask questions

title: Women
content:
The women’s ministry exists to transform women’s lives through relationships with Jesus Christ and with one another:

  • to actively promote love among all women with the love of Christ through the power of the Spirit.
  • to provide meaningful opportunities for all women to grow individually and communally.
  • to serve God through support of the various ministries offer in All Saints’ Church for the expansion of His kingdom and to the glory of God the Father.

This year we are focusing on healing and building relationships by:

  • emphasizing His unmerited grace towards us in calling us each to be his daughter (reconciliation with God: 2 Corinthians 5:18–21; Colossians 1:21–23)
  • experiencing the inner healing that flows out of knowing we are each His beloved child (reconciliation with ourselves: Isaiah 61:1–2b; Psalm 34:18; Jeremiah 30); and
  • loving and learning to forgive each other as we are loved and forgiven (reconciliation with each other: Matthew 5:23–24; 1 Corinthians 1:10–11; Corinthians 13:4-7).

Contact: The Rev. Julie Tilton, jtilton@allsaintswoodbridge.org

Vision

Dorcas Ministry

The Dorcas Ministry meets on the first Saturday of the month, October through June, in the middle school classroom (lower level in the right back corner of the Multi-Purpose Room) from 9:30-11 a.m. Bring crocheting, knitting, sewing, and other items to work on while we are gathered, as well as items you have completed. We will bless and collect completed items for distribution to the poor, the sick, and the needy.

Why “Dorcas Ministry”? Dorcas was a disciple of Jesus and lived in the town of Joppa, a city on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. She was a charitable person who made things for the needy. You can read about her in Acts 9:36-42, including Peter’s restoration of her life.

Email Emily Fawcett at emilymfawcett@gmail.com to get on the mailing list to keep updated on changes in meetings and other opportunities.

title: Give
content:
There are multiple ways to make a financial gift to All Saints’ Church. You can mail a check to the church (14851 Gideon Drive Woodbridge, VA 22192) or drop off a check at the church office. You can also submit your donation online or use “text” to make your donation!

Online givers now have the option to increase their donation amount in order to help offset costs for our church. The donor is always credited the full amount given. For instance, someone making a $100 credit card donation will have the option to add $3.30 to their donation. That person will be credited with a $103.30 contribution. For an ACH bank transfer directly from a checking account, the processing fee for $100 is less at $1.26.
